title: Evidence & citations
failFast: Answer has no concrete file paths under codebasePath (and no db: citations when only config is relevant) → score < 90
Citations cannot be located or do not support the claim → score < 90

rubric.90: Every material claim is backed by a real file/path, db: citation, and/or skill ref
rubric.70: Mostly cited; a few soft claims lack pointers
rubric.40: Thin evidence; heavy reliance on general knowledge

prompt.task: Score whether the answer is grounded in real codebase, skill, and live-config sources
instructions: Require citations: repo-relative paths under codebasePath (prefer path + symbol/class or short quote)
Accept live-config citations of the form db:<connection>/<database>.<table>#<key> when domain has configSources
Open cited files and verify they exist and support the claim; for db: citations require matching configLookups
Skill pointers used should be named when domain docs were relied on
Apply failFast and rubric
Score 0-100; 90+ means a human can re-check the answer from citations alone

title: Faithfulness to sources
failFast: Any claim contradicts the cited code, live config, or domain CONTEXT → score < 90
Answer invents APIs/services/flags not present in sources → score < 90
Answer treats Java code defaults as production truth when live config was checked and differs → score < 90

rubric.90: Claims match cited sources (code + config); no inventing

prompt.task: Score whether the answer faithfully reflects the codebase, live config, and domain CONTEXT
instructions: Compare each key claim to cited files, configLookups, and domainContext
Flag hallucinations, outdated assumptions, and conflated services
If configLookups exist, answers must not contradict them
Uncertainty must be labeled as such — guessing without a citation fails
Apply failFast and rubric
Score 0-100; 90+ means trustworthy for operational decisions

title: Answers the question
failFast: Critical related path (e.g. call chain) omitted when the question asks how it works → score < 90

rubric.90: Directly answers the question with enough depth for a teammate to act
rubric.70: Mostly answers; missing secondary but useful detail

prompt.task: Score whether the answer fully addresses the user's question
instructions: Check the question is answered head-on, not only adjacent trivia
For how-it-works questions expect flow: entry → key components → data/control path
When runtime flags matter, completeness includes stating code default vs live overrides
Apply failFast and rubric
Score 0-100; 90+ means ready to share with confidence

title: Live config / flags verified
failFast: domainContext.hasLiveConfig and answer asserts production/runtime flag behavior without configLookups → score < 90
Known flag-gated claim (enablement, caps, thresholds, similar-articles, fail-fast) cites only code default and ignores configSources → score < 90
configLookups report values that contradict the answer prose → score < 90
Invented DB rows / attribute names not in configSources or code → score < 90

rubric.90: Flag-sensitive claims checked against live config (or explicitly marked unchecked with why)
rubric.70: Partial lookup; missing an important related attribute
rubric.40: Relies on code defaults as if they were prod truth
rubric.0: Ignores configSources entirely on a flag-gated question

prompt.task: Score whether runtime/publisher/common config was verified when it can change the answer
instructions: Read domainContext.configSources (stores, knownAttributes, queryRules, citationFormat)
If hasLiveConfig is false or stores empty: score 100 with summary 'N/A — no config sources for domain'
If the question/answer is pure code structure with no flag effect: score 90+ only if answer correctly says config is irrelevant (or still did a quick knownAttributes check)
Otherwise require configLookups (SQL + connection + result summary) and db: citations
Distinguish: (1) Java Proxy fallback, (2) common.config setting, (3) publisher_config override
Re-query or demand re-query if lookups are missing for attributes named in the answer
Apply failFast and rubric
Score 0-100; 90+ means a teammate would not be misled by stale flag assumptions
